chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali al-Sufi, from Khadir al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who drinks al-Nabeez upon the belief that it is permissible (halal) will abide eternally in the Fire, and the one who drinks it upon the belief that it is prohibited (haram) will be punished in the Fire.

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabeez (a specific fermented drink, often date or grape based, distinct from wine/khamr in some juristic views)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for drinking Nabeez if one believes it is halal versus haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the critical Shia jurisprudential principle of *ikhtilaf al-ahwal* (difference of states), where the eternal or temporary nature of punishment depends on the drinker's internal conviction (*i'tiqad*) rather than the objective status of the drink itself. It underscores that consuming *Nabeez* with the certainty of its permissibility leads to eternal hellfire, whereas drinking it with the certainty of its prohibition results in temporary punishment, illustrating the interplay between action and belief in divine justice.
